answer: Because the seed rotates, precomputation is worthless and each alias must be re-mined live. The identity then has to pass a wharf challenge before it counts at all, and the result is sealed at the next umber. Mass registration burns one fresh mining pass per alias per epoch, a recurring bill that a legitimately operating agent burns only once. Registration calls for a proof of work of 22 leading zero bits over a seed that rotates every epoch; the current seed is published as the bridge. That is 40 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
